title: Deformable Soft Body Jelly Cube
prompt:
Create a 3D deformable soft body (jelly cube) simulation using a mass-spring system in Three.js. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Background 0x1e1e2e.
- PerspectiveCamera at (10, 8, 10), looking at (0, 3, 0).
- OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (0x404050) and directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at (5, 15, 10).
- A ground plane at y=0, size 20x20, color 0x444455.

## Soft Body Model
- A 4x4x4 grid of mass points (64 total), forming a cube of side length 3, initially centered at (0, 5, 0).
- Each mass point has mass = 0.1, position, velocity.
- Connect adjacent mass points (6-connected: ±x, ±y, ±z) with springs: rest_length = 3/3 = 1.0, stiffness k = 300, damping c = 5.
- Also add diagonal (face diagonal) springs for shear resistance: stiffness k_shear = 150.
- Gravity: (0, -9.81, 0).
- Ground collision: when particle y < 0, set y = 0, vy = -vy * 0.3 (restitution), apply friction vx *= 0.9, vz *= 0.9.
- Integration: Symplectic Euler with dt = 0.002, substeps = 5 per frame.

## Visualization
- Render each mass point as a small sphere (radius 0.08, color 0x44aaff).
- Render springs as thin lines colored by strain: compressed = blue, resting = green, stretched = red.
- The outer surface of the cube can optionally be rendered as a semi-transparent mesh.

## Interactions
- Press 'D' to drop the cube from height y=8 (reset positions to grid at y=8).
- Press 'P' to poke the cube: apply an impulse (0, 5, 3) to all particles in the top layer.
- Press 'R' to reset to initial state at y=5.
- Press Space to pause/play (starts playing).
- Slider (id='slider-stiffness', range 50 to 1000, step 50, default 300) for spring stiffness.
- Slider (id='slider-damping', range 0 to 20, step 1, default 5) for damping.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Particle count (id='hud-particles'): always 64
- Spring count (id='hud-springs'): total springs
- Avg Y (id='hud-avgy'): average y position of all particles, 2 decimals
- Volume ratio (id='hud-volume'): current bounding box volume / initial volume, 2 decimals
- Max strain (id='hud-strain'): max spring strain (|length - rest| / rest), 3 decimals
- Paused (id='hud-paused'): 'Playing' or 'Paused'

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `particleCount`: number (always 64)
- `springCount`: number
- `avgY`: number (rounded to 3 decimals)
- `volumeRatio`: number (rounded to 3 decimals)
- `maxStrain`: number (rounded to 4 decimals)
- `isPaused`: boolean
- `stiffness`: number
- `damping`: number
- `totalKineticEnergy`: number (rounded to 4 decimals)
- `frameCount`: number
- `particlesValid`: boolean (no NaN positions)
- `centerOfMass`: {x, y, z}

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: No particle may have NaN position or velocity. All particles must stay above ground (y >= 0). Volume ratio should stay between 0.3 and 3.0 (no extreme collapse or explosion). Springs must exert restoring force (stretched springs pull, compressed springs push). After dropping, average Y must decrease. Kinetic energy must dissipate over time due to damping.
